observation_summary: The ValueMarker constructor was incorrectly passing the paint and stroke parameters to the superclass constructor instead of the outlinePaint and outlineStroke parameters, causing the marker to be rendered with the wrong colors.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves correcting the arguments passed to the superclass constructor in the ValueMarker class. The original code incorrectly used the primary paint and stroke for the outline properties. This is a classic case of incorrect initialization of an object's state via its constructor parameters.
evidence_used: fix_diff_oracle: - super(paint, stroke, paint, stroke, alpha); + super(paint, stroke, outlinePaint, outlineStroke, alpha);

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix changes a method call (the super constructor), the root cause is the incorrect assignment of values to the object's internal state (the outline properties) during initialization.
